headline: NIFTY & BEYOND
standfirst: What the index doesn't tell you · Weekly Wrap · 31 August – 5 September 2026
s1_summary_note: Across the week of 31 August to 5 September 2026, Indian equities consolidated in a narrow 1.15% range as Nifty closed at 23,897.70. Underneath, domestic institutions mounted a record weekly buying offensive (+₹23,156 Cr), absorbing heavy FII cash liquidation (-₹5,612 Cr). Sector rotation favored Energy and Banking, while a single corporate announcement by UltraTech Cement into wires & cables repriced the entire industrial capital goods space.

s1_bullets.label: Index Weekly Performance
s1_bullets.text: Nifty 50 closed at 23,897.70 (-1.15% 1W), Sensex at 76,515.43 (-0.95% 1W), and Nifty Bank at 57,369.65 (-0.02% 1W), holding key structural support.

s1_bullets.label: Weekly Breadth & Participation
s1_bullets.text: Nifty 500 advance/decline ratio averaged 0.88 across the week; 34% of constituents trade above their 20-day SMA while Smallcaps outperformed (+0.08% 1W).

s1_bullets.label: Record Weekly DII Cash Buying
s1_bullets.text: Domestic institutions poured in a record +₹23,156.26 Cr cash net buy over 5 sessions, absorbing 412% of foreign institutional cash sales (-₹5,612.00 Cr).

s1_bullets.label: Industry Disruption
s1_bullets.text: UltraTech's entry into wires & cables ('Ultravolt' brand with ₹1,800 Cr capex) triggered an aggressive weekly selloff in KEI (-12.9% 1W), RR Kabel (-15.5% 1W), Polycab (-8.7% 1W), and Havells (-8.0% 1W).

s1_bullets.label: Tijori Operational Intel
s1_bullets.text: Realty standout Brigade launched 'Brigade Barcelona' (₹2,700 Cr GDV); Tijori metrics confirm ₹12,915/sqft realization, 30.87M sqft pipeline, and 76% hotel occupancy.

s1_bullets.label: Fear Gauge & Volatility
s1_bullets.text: India VIX fell to 10.62 — a six-week low (82nd percentile calm), with weekly put writers moving defensive lines up 300 points to 23,900 at the money.

s1_commodities_source: MCX EOD & Bloomberg Weekly Spot Rates

s2_glosses.Breadth: Weekly percentage of Nifty 500 stocks trading above their 50-day average stands at 42.4% (ranked 59 of 250 sessions). Over 57% of the universe remains technically below medium-term moving averages, confirming that broad market participation has not yet repaired despite Friday's index rebound.
s2_glosses.Trend: Nifty 50 sits 2.9% below its 200-day moving average on a weekly basis. Remaining below this key structural barrier confirms that long-term technical resistance persists and the burden of proof sits squarely with the bulls on any recovery.
s2_glosses.Momentum: Weekly A/D ratio averaged 0.88 across the week (ranked 116 of 246 sessions). Momentum surged on Wednesday (+1.51 A/D) before fading into Friday as traders squared positions ahead of US economic data.
s2_glosses.InstitutionalFlow: Extreme weekly institutional divergence: FIIs recorded heavy weekly cash selling (-₹5,612 Cr) while DIIs executed record weekly cash buying (+₹23,156 Cr). DIIs absorbed 412% of FII selling across the week, mounting an unprecedented structural floor.
s2_glosses.Volatility: Nifty ATR is compressed at 0.74% of price (calmer than 82% of sessions, ranked 45 of 250). Weekly volatility compression below the 200D SMA is a classic coiling signature that typically precedes a sharp macro-driven breakout.

s2_composition_note: The weekly Market Regime score of 45.3 (Neutral) reflects a 46.9-point spread between the weakest component (Breadth at 35.3) and the strongest (Volatility at 82.2). Excluding Volatility, the core weekly score drops to 41.3 (Weak Neutral). The weekly headline score reflects a market that is technically capped below its 200D SMA with weak medium-term breadth, but aggressively cushioned by record DII weekly cash absorption (+₹23,156 Cr) and volatility compression ahead of US payrolls.

s3_anomalies.title: Domestic Buying at Record Weekly High (+₹23,156 Cr)
s3_anomalies.text: Domestic institutions executed a record weekly net cash purchase of ₹23,156 crore across 5 sessions — by far the largest weekly allocation in our 39-session database, absorbing 412% of FII cash liquidation (-₹5,612 Cr).

s3_anomalies.title: NIACL — +23.4% 1W Breakout on NSE IPO Anticipation
s3_anomalies.text: Surged 23.4% over the week to a 52-week high of ₹229.30 on 7.6x volume (RSI 78.7 overbought, ADX 39.6). Driven by market pricing in value unlock from its 1.42% corporate equity stake in the upcoming NSE IPO.

s3_anomalies.title: KEI Industries — -12.9% 1W Cable De-Rating (Tijori Industry Intel)
s3_anomalies.text: Plunged 12.9% over the week on 5.5x volume (-12.8% below 20SMA, RSI 34) alongside Polycab (-8.7% 1W) and RR Kabel (-15.5% 1W). Triggered by UltraTech Cement's aggressive ₹1,800 Cr entry into wires & cables ('Ultravolt' brand). Tijori data shows Finolex & KEI communication cable realizations at ₹2,204/km across 2.63M km annual sales; UltraTech's entrance threatens long-term pricing power.

s3_anomalies.title: HBL Engineering — 12.3x Weekly Volume Expansion
s3_anomalies.text: Recorded the highest weekly volume multiple at 12.3x normal volume for a modest 3.2% weekly price gain. Indicates massive institutional block transfers rather than retail momentum.

s3_anomalies.title: Tejas Networks — +11.6% 1W Rally on ₹1,537 Cr BSNL Order
s3_anomalies.text: Gained 11.6% over the week on 6x volume (+15.4% above 20SMA, RSI 72.3). Powered by TCS's ₹1,537 Cr LOI for BSNL 4G/5G Radio Access Network equipment supply. Tijori metrics highlight R&D reinvestment held at 5.63% of sales and 3.82x net sales per employee cost ratio.

s3_anomalies.title: Brigade Enterprises — +8.4% 1W Expansion on Tijori Operational Strength
s3_anomalies.text: Gained 8.4% over the week following the announcement of 'Brigade Barcelona' in Hyderabad Neopolis corridor (₹2,700 Cr GDV). Tijori operational metrics confirm strong fundamental backing: ₹12,915/sqft realization, 30.87M sqft area under construction, 76% hotel occupancy with ₹7,241 ADR (RevPAR ₹5,503), and 7.61% borrowing cost.

s3_anomalies.title: Solar Industries — Tijori Order Book Intel (145.5% of Sales)
s3_anomalies.text: Maintained institutional focus amid South Africa acquisition clarifications. Tijori metrics reveal bulk explosives realization of ₹47,340/MT across 5.88L tonnes annual volume, with defense & commercial order book standing at 145.5% of annual revenue.

s3_anomalies.title: Nifty Oil & Gas — 27-Point Weekly Breadth Swing
s3_anomalies.text: The share of Nifty Oil and Gas constituents above their 20-day average rose 27 percentage points over 5 sessions (best weekly sector performer at +1.08% 1W), as Brent crude held near $95 and refining margins firmed.

s3_anomalies.title: Nifty FMCG — 0% Stocks >20D SMA for 2 Consecutive Weeks
s3_anomalies.text: FMCG sector ended the week with zero of fifteen constituents trading above their 20-day SMA (-2.0% 1W, -7.34% 1M). Demonstrates a persistent structural drawdown in consumer staples.

s3_anomalies.title: India VIX — 10.62 Six-Week Low Compression
s3_anomalies.text: India VIX fell to 10.62 (82nd percentile calm) despite ongoing Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions, creating extreme volatility compression.

s4_macro_cards.title: Domestic Monetary Policy, Rates & Liquidity (Top 50 Macro #1 – #6)
s4_macro_cards.meta: RBI MPC · Net LAF Liquidity · 10Y Sovereign Yield
bullets: RBI Repo Rate & MPC Stance (#1): Held steady at 6.50% with hawkish stance ('withdrawal of accommodation'). Minutes highlight inflation persistence concerns.
10-Year Sovereign G-Sec Yield (#4): Traded at 6.94%, anchoring domestic borrowing costs as the risk-free rate.
Bank Credit vs Deposit Growth Gap (#3): Credit growth ran at 14.2% YoY while deposit growth lagged at 10.8% YoY, maintaining margin pressure on banks and driving CD issuance.
Daily Systemic Liquidity (#2): Net LAF operations maintained a comfortable ₹42,000 Cr liquidity surplus in the banking system.

s4_macro_cards.meta: MoSPI · S&P Global · DPIIT Eight Core Index
bullets: S&P Global Manufacturing PMI (#12): Printed strong at 57.5, signaling active factory order expansion and sustained job creation.
S&P Global Services PMI (#13): Extended robust urban expansion to 60.9, confirming resilient domestic consumption.

CPI Inflation Trajectory (#7): Headline inflation moderated to 3.54% YoY, staying within RBI's 4.0% (+/- 2%) target band.

s4_macro_cards.meta: Auto Dispatches · GST Collections · IMD Monsoon

Auto OEM Factory Dispatches (#14): August dispatches showed festive stocking: Maruti Suzuki 1.76L units, TVS Motors 4.33L units, Hero MotoCorp 5.42L units.
IMD Southwest Monsoon (#19): Cumulative rainfall stood at +7% surplus above Normal, boosting Kharif acreage and rural discretionary outlook.

s4_macro_cards.title: Capital Flows, Fiscal Health & FX Reserves (Top 50 Macro #21 – #32)
s4_macro_cards.meta: FPI/DII Cash · AMFI SIP Inflows · RBI FX Reserves
bullets: RBI Forex Reserves (#30): Expanded $11.475 billion in a single week to a record high $740.803 billion, providing an unshakeable currency buffer.

AMFI Monthly SIP Inflows (#26): Monthly SIP contributions hit a record ₹23,332 Cr, supplying a steady ₹1,100 Cr daily domestic liquidity cushion.
Merchandise Trade & CAD (#28, #29): Trade deficit narrowed to $23.5Bn; Current Account Deficit remains comfortable at 1.1% of GDP.

s4_macro_cards.meta: US Fed · DXY · Brent Crude · China PMI

Brent Crude & OPEC+ (#47, #48): Brent firmed to $95.23/bbl on Hormuz transit friction and OPEC+ production caps.

s5_global.signal: Rate-hike fears eased Friday after Fed governor Waller noted improving inflation.
Recovered late-week losses; remains in a broader weekly trading range.
Hormuz traffic remains reduced; oil sits near multi-week highs.
Yield curve easing supports foreign capital allocation into emerging markets.
Rupee strength supported by record RBI forex reserves ($740.8Bn).
Safe-haven bid unwound late in the week.

s5_timing_note:
Timing matters. US markets close after India's. Wall Street figures reflect weekly closes — they provided the cue for Friday's open, and next week's US session is the cue for Monday. Brent, gold, silver and the rupee trade through Indian hours.

The transmission chain, named. Over the week, global market signals traveled into India along three paths. First, into the open: US rate-hike fears eased Friday, Wall Street bounced, and Nifty futures moved from short buildup to short covering. Second, into currency: softer dollar expectations combined with record RBI reserves ($740.8Bn) allowed India to absorb $95 crude without currency depreciation. Third, into safe havens: gold (-1.86% 1W) and silver (-1.64% 1W) unwound safe-haven bids. Where the chain did not reach is domestic consumer breadth — 264 shares fell Friday, FMCG remained at 0% >20D, and Auto breadth dropped 46 points over 5 sessions.
s6_note: Over one week the weekly board was uniformly negative except smallcaps — Nifty 50 down 1.15%, Next 50 down 1.72%, Midcap 100 down 1.55%, while Smallcap 100 gained 0.08%. The Nifty's own weekly range was tight and unconvincing: it opened at 23,910.90, reached 24,005.75, and closed at 23,897.70 — below its open, in the lower third of a 109.9-point daily range that was the narrowest in weeks.
s7_note:
Eight sectors moved enough in weekly breadth to flag. They split into a banking-and-energy group that is quietly strengthening and a manufacturing-and-defensive group that is deteriorating fast.

NIFTY IT — worst breadth for a second consecutive session: 0.25 A/D, share above 20D SMA dropped 40 points in 3 sessions to 30%. Index down 1.88% over the week.

NIFTY HEALTHCARE — breadth of 0.18, worse than IT. Share above 20D SMA at 25% after 20-point drop; index down 2.32% 1W.

NIFTY PSU BANK — share above 20D SMA rose 25 points in 3 sessions to 50%, a clear positive rotation.

NIFTY CAPITAL GOODS — dramatic reversal. Flipped from +14 to -12 on 5-day breadth due to UltraTech cable entry.

NIFTY REALTY — profit taking after a vertical move. Down 0.90% Friday but up 18.74% over 3 months.

NIFTY AUTO — most damaged sector. A/D 0.15, just 7% above 20D SMA, down 46 points of breadth in 5 sessions (-3.95% 1W).

NIFTY METAL — best sector Friday (+1.07%), 53% above 20D SMA.

NIFTY FMCG — second week with 0% of constituents above 20D SMA (-2.0% 1W, -7.34% 1M).
s8_implication: The weekly rotation has sharpened into a simple macro thesis: money is moving into banks and energy, and out of manufacturing and defensives. Banking and Oil & Gas dominate weekly breadth gains; Auto, Consumer Durables, Healthcare, and IT dominate weekly breadth losses. That is a bet on domestic credit growth and high energy prices, funded by selling consumer and tech exposure.
s9_note: Weekly scanner extremes were dominated by two stories. On the upside, NIACL (+23.4% 1W) and IFCI (+12.7% 1W) traded on NSE IPO valuation unlocks. On the downside, KEI (-12.9% 1W), RR Kabel (-15.5% 1W), Polycab (-8.7% 1W), and Havells (-8.0% 1W) were hit by UltraTech's entry.

s10_triggers.text: UltraTech Cement launched Ultravolt, taking Aditya Birla Group into wires & cables with ₹1,800 Cr capex. Tijori data shows Finolex & KEI communication cable realizations at ₹2,204/km across 2.63M km annual sales; UltraTech's entrance threatens long-term pricing power.
Anticipation of National Stock Exchange (NSE) IPO. NIACL rose 23.4% 1W to ₹229.30 on 7.6x volume; IFCI rose alongside it. Both hold corporate equity stakes in the exchange.
Powered by TCS's ₹1,537 Cr LOI for BSNL 4G/5G Radio Access Network equipment supply. Tijori operational metrics highlight Tejas maintaining R&D investments at 5.63% of total sales.

Enriched via Tijori operational feeds. Brigade announced 'Brigade Barcelona' (₹2,700 Cr GDV) with Tijori metrics confirming ₹12,915/sqft realization and 30.87M sqft under construction; Balrampur Chini navigates 2,000 qtl sugar stock limits with 9.62% sugar recovery rate; Solar Industries maintains 145.5% order book to sales ratio.

watch.confirms: Holding it keeps 12.63 million put contracts in profit and the market pinned in its 100-point box into Tuesday's expiry. Put writers moved their floor up 300 points to get here — they will defend it.
watch.denies: Losing it turns the largest put position in the chain into a forced unwind.

watch.item: Whether weekly breadth can hold above 1.0
watch.confirms: Two good weeks in a row would be the first evidence the broad market is participating rather than oscillating.
watch.denies: Sub-1.0 breadth with index gains means the advance keeps narrowing into fewer names.

watch.confirms: One stock in fifteen above 20D SMA is near the floor. Any recovery relieves the worst-damaged sector.
watch.denies: Auto has lost 46 points of breadth in 5 sessions. Continued falls make it a structural consumption problem.

watch.confirms: Stabilization in KEI / Polycab signals limited short-term margin erosion.
watch.denies: Further falls signal market re-examining every business where Aditya Birla Group could enter next.

s14.closing: Across the week of 31 August to 5 September 2026, Indian equities consolidated in a narrow range with Nifty closing down 1.15% at 23,897.70. Underneath, domestic institutions mounted an unprecedented ₹23,156 Cr cash buying offensive, insulating the market from FII sales (-₹5,612 Cr). With options put writers defending 23,900 at the money and VIX compressed to 10.62, position carefully into next week's inflation print and Fed rate decision.
